decisions.quote: Using a database built to simulate the size of the L2 English mental lexicon, we found larger counts of both pseudo-homophones and pseudo-phonological neighbors for /l/-/r/ misperception than /ɛ/-/ae/. Compared to Cutler (2005), we found fewer pseudo-homophones in terms of raw numbers, but a larger proportion of the L2 lexicon becomes homophonous for each misperception pattern.
decisions.reason: The study confirms Cutler's (2005) core finding that /l/-/r/ misperception produces substantially more pseudo-homophones than /ɛ/-/ae/ misperception. The lower raw counts and higher lexicon proportions reflect the deliberately tenfold smaller L2 vocabulary database relative to Cutler's 70,000-word CELEX upper bound rather than conflicting replication results.
